stem.en: Pneumatophores, roots that grow upward for respiration, are found in:

explanation.en: Mangroves like Rhizophora in swampy soil form pneumatophores.

stem.en: Stilt roots arising from the lower nodes of the stem are found in:

explanation.en: Maize and sugarcane have supporting stilt roots from lower nodes.

stem.en: Root hairs develop from the:

explanation.en: Epidermal cells in the region of maturation form root hairs.

stem.en: The fibrous root system is seen in:

explanation.en: In monocots like wheat, the primary root is replaced by many roots from the stem base.

solution.en: In monocots like wheat, the primary root is replaced by many roots from the stem base.

stem.en: Sweet potato stores food in its:

explanation.en: NCERT: adventitious roots of sweet potato get swollen and store food. (Potato, by contrast, is a stem tuber.)

stem.en: The potato is a modified:

explanation.en: The potato is a stem tuber: its eyes are nodes with buds.

stem.en: Stem tendrils of cucumber and pumpkin develop from:

explanation.en: Stem tendrils develop from axillary buds.

stem.en: Thorns of Citrus and Bougainvillea are modified:

explanation.en: These thorns are stem structures arising from axillary buds.

stem.en: The flattened green stem that carries out photosynthesis in arid conditions is seen in:

explanation.en: Opuntia has a flattened stem; Euphorbia has a fleshy cylindrical one.

solution.en: Opuntia has a flattened stem; Euphorbia has a fleshy cylindrical one.

stem.en: A lateral branch with short internodes, each node bearing a rosette of leaves and a tuft of roots, is found in:

explanation.en: This is an offset, seen in aquatic plants like Pistia and Eichhornia.

stem.en: A swollen leaf base called the pulvinus is seen in:

explanation.en: In some leguminous plants the leaf base is swollen into a pulvinus.

stem.en: Whorled phyllotaxy is seen in:

explanation.en: Alstonia has more than two leaves at each node in a whorl.

stem.en: An example of a palmately compound leaf is:

explanation.en: In silk cotton the leaflets are attached at a common point at the tip of the petiole.

stem.en: Leaves are modified into tendrils in:

explanation.en: In pea, leaflets are modified into tendrils for climbing.

solution.en: In pea, leaflets are modified into tendrils for climbing.

stem.en: A pinnately compound leaf is distinguished from a twig bearing simple leaves because:

options.en: A bud is present in the axil of the petiole but not in the axils of the leaflets

explanation.en: Buds occur in the axil of the whole leaf (petiole), never in the axils of leaflets.

stem.en: In a racemose inflorescence:

options.en: The main axis ends in a flower
The main axis continues to grow and flowers are borne in acropetal succession

explanation.en: In racemose inflorescences the axis keeps growing; older flowers are below, younger above.

stem.en: A zygomorphic flower is found in:

explanation.en: Pea flowers can be divided into two equal halves only in one vertical plane.

stem.en: A perigynous flower, with a half-inferior ovary, is seen in:

explanation.en: Plum, rose and peach are perigynous; guava and cucumber are epigynous.

stem.en: Twisted aestivation is found in:

explanation.en: China rose, lady's finger and cotton show twisted aestivation.

solution.en: China rose, lady's finger and cotton show twisted aestivation.

stem.en: In vexillary aestivation, the largest petal that overlaps the two lateral petals is the:

explanation.en: The largest posterior petal is the standard (vexillum); the two smallest anterior petals form the keel.

stem.en: Diadelphous stamens, united in two bundles, are found in:

explanation.en: Pea has stamens in two bundles (9 + 1).

stem.en: Axile placentation is seen in:

explanation.en: China rose, tomato and lemon have axile placentation.

stem.en: Free central placentation is found in:

explanation.en: In Dianthus and Primrose, ovules are borne on a central axis without septa.

stem.en: Stamens attached to the perianth (epiphyllous) are found in:

explanation.en: Lily has epiphyllous stamens; brinjal has epipetalous stamens.

solution.en: Lily has epiphyllous stamens; brinjal has epipetalous stamens.

stem.en: Placentation in which the ovary becomes two-chambered due to a false septum, with ovules on the inner wall, is found in:

explanation.en: This is parietal placentation, as in mustard and Argemone.

stem.en: The edible part of a mango is the:

explanation.en: The fleshy mesocarp of the mango drupe is eaten.

stem.en: In the maize grain, the single large shield-shaped cotyledon is called the:

explanation.en: The scutellum is the cotyledon of the maize embryo.

stem.en: The coleoptile in a monocot seed encloses the:

explanation.en: The plumule is enclosed by the coleoptile; the radicle by the coleorhiza.

stem.en: The floral formula ⊕ P(3+3) A3+3 G(3) represents the family:

explanation.en: Six tepals in two whorls, six stamens and a tricarpellary ovary are typical of Liliaceae.

solution.en: Six tepals in two whorls, six stamens and a tricarpellary ovary are typical of Liliaceae.

stem.en: A family with zygomorphic flowers, diadelphous stamens (9) + 1 and a monocarpellary ovary with marginal placentation is:

explanation.en: These are the floral features of Fabaceae (pea family).

stem.en:
Assertion (A): Potato is a modified root that stores food.
Reason (R): The potato tuber bears nodes, the 'eyes', from which buds arise.

options.en: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

explanation.en: A is false: the potato is a stem tuber, not a root. R is true, and the eyes (nodes with buds) are the very evidence that it is a stem.

passage.en: On a visit to the mangrove forest near Kundapura, students see that the mud is waterlogged and smells of rotting matter; the soil water holds very little oxygen. From the mud around Rhizophora trees, many finger-like roots grow vertically upwards and stick out above the soil.

stem.en: These upward-growing roots mainly help the plant by:

options.en: storing food during the dry season

explanation.en: In swampy plants like Rhizophora, pneumatophores grow upwards above the ground and help the roots get oxygen for respiration.

stem.en:
Assertion (A): Pea shows marginal placentation.
Reason (R): In marginal placentation the placenta forms a ridge along the ventral suture of the ovary, and the ovules are borne on this ridge in two rows.

options.en: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

explanation.en: Both are true; R describes marginal placentation, which is exactly the arrangement in the pea pod.

passage.en: Shreya slices a young lemon across its middle. She sees that the ovary has several chambers (locules) separated by thin walls. All the seeds are attached in the centre, where the walls meet along the central axis of the fruit.

stem.en: The type of placentation in the lemon is:

explanation.en: When the placenta is axial and the ovules are attached to it in a multilocular ovary, the placentation is axile, as in lemon, tomato and china rose.

stem.en:
Match the root modification with the plant:
a. Pneumatophores  b. Prop roots  c. Stilt roots  d. Adventitious storage roots
(i) Banyan  (ii) Rhizophora  (iii) Sweet potato  (iv) Maize

explanation.en: Rhizophora has pneumatophores, banyan has prop roots, maize has stilt roots, and sweet potato stores food in adventitious roots.

solution.en: Rhizophora has pneumatophores, banyan has prop roots, maize has stilt roots, and sweet potato stores food in adventitious roots.

stem.en: Which one of the following is NOT a modified stem?

explanation.en: Sweet potato is a swollen adventitious root. The potato tuber, the ginger rhizome and the thorns of Bougainvillea are all stem modifications.

stem.en:
Match the type of aestivation with the plant:
a. Valvate  b. Twisted  c. Imbricate  d. Vexillary
(i) Cassia  (ii) Pea  (iii) Calotropis  (iv) Cotton

explanation.en: Calotropis is valvate, cotton twisted, Cassia imbricate and pea vexillary.

solution.en: Calotropis is valvate, cotton twisted, Cassia imbricate and pea vexillary.

stem.en: Which pair is correctly matched?

explanation.en: Pea has diadelphous stamens (9 + 1). China rose is monoadelphous, Citrus polyadelphous, and brinjal has epipetalous stamens.

stem.en:
Assertion (A): The mango is a drupe.
Reason (R): It develops from a monocarpellary superior ovary and is one-seeded.

options.en: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

explanation.en: Both are true and R explains A: a drupe is a one-seeded fruit from a monocarpellary superior ovary, with a stony endocarp, as in mango and coconut.

stem.en: The primary root of a dicot plant develops from the:

explanation.en: In most dicotyledonous plants the direct elongation of the radicle leads to the formation of the primary root, which grows inside the soil and bears lateral roots of several orders (tap root system). The stem develops from the plumule.

stem.en: A fibrous root system is found in:

explanation.en: In monocotyledonous plants like wheat, the primary root is short-lived and is replaced by a large number of roots originating from the base of the stem — the fibrous root system. Mustard has a tap root; carrot and turnip have swollen tap roots storing food.

stem.en: Pneumatophores, roots that grow vertically upwards to obtain oxygen, are found in:

explanation.en: In plants such as Rhizophora growing in swampy areas, many roots come out of the ground and grow vertically upwards (pneumatophores) to get oxygen for respiration. Banyan has prop roots, maize has stilt roots and sweet potato has adventitious roots swollen with food.

stem.en: Which of these is an underground stem modified for storage?

explanation.en: Potato is an underground stem (tuber) — it has nodes (eyes) bearing buds. Carrot and turnip are modified tap roots, and sweet potato is a modified adventitious root. Ginger, turmeric, zaminkand and Colocasia are other underground stems.

stem.en: Thorns of Citrus and Bougainvillea are modifications of:

explanation.en: Axillary buds of stems may get modified into woody, straight and pointed thorns, as in Citrus and Bougainvillea. They protect plants from browsing animals. The spines of cacti, in contrast, are modified leaves.

stem.en: In a pinnately compound leaf such as that of neem, the leaflets are present on a common axis called the:

explanation.en: In a pinnately compound leaf a number of leaflets are present on a common axis, the rachis, which represents the midrib of the leaf, as in neem. In palmately compound leaves (silk cotton) the leaflets are attached at a common point — the tip of the petiole. A pulvinus is a swollen leaf base.

stem.en: Whorled phyllotaxy (more than two leaves at a node) is seen in:

explanation.en: In Alstonia, more than two leaves arise at a node and form a whorl — whorled phyllotaxy. China rose and mustard show alternate phyllotaxy; guava and Calotropis show opposite phyllotaxy.

stem.en: Leaves of onion and garlic are modified for:

explanation.en: The fleshy leaves of onion and garlic store food. Leaves are modified into tendrils for climbing (peas) and into spines for defence (cacti).

stem.en: When calyx and corolla are not distinct, they are together termed:

explanation.en: When calyx and corolla are not distinct they are termed perianth, as in lily. The thalamus (receptacle) bears the floral whorls; a bract is a reduced leaf at the base of the pedicel.

stem.en: Stamens attached to the petals are called:

explanation.en: When stamens are attached to the petals they are epipetalous, as in brinjal. When attached to the perianth they are epiphyllous (lily). A sterile stamen is a staminode; diadelphous means stamens united in two bundles.

stem.en: In a seed, the scar through which the developing seed was attached to the fruit is the:

explanation.en: The hilum is a scar on the seed coat through which the developing seed was attached to the fruit. Above the hilum is a small pore, the micropyle. Testa and tegmen are the outer and inner layers of the seed coat.

stem.en: Fabaceae was earlier called:

explanation.en: Fabaceae was earlier called Papilionoideae, a subfamily of family Leguminosae. It is distributed all over the world.

stem.en: The region of a root responsible for its growth in length is the:

explanation.en: Cells proximal to the meristematic region undergo rapid elongation and enlargement and are responsible for the growth of the root in length — the region of elongation. The meristematic region (a few mm above the root cap) divides repeatedly; the region of maturation bears root hairs; the root cap protects the tender apex.

stem.en: Stilt roots that arise from the lower nodes of the stem and give support are found in:

explanation.en: In maize and sugarcane the supporting roots coming out of the lower nodes of the stem are called stilt roots. Banyan has hanging prop roots from branches; Rhizophora has pneumatophores; Monstera has adventitious roots.

stem.en: Stem tendrils that develop from axillary buds are found in:

explanation.en: Stem tendrils develop from axillary buds, are slender and spirally coiled, and help plants to climb, as in gourds (cucumber, pumpkins, watermelon) and grapevines. In pea, the tendrils are modified leaves (leaflets). Citrus has thorns; Opuntia has a flattened photosynthetic stem.

stem.en: In aquatic plants like Pistia and Eichhornia, vegetative propagation occurs by:

explanation.en: In aquatic plants like Pistia and Eichhornia, a lateral branch with short internodes, each node bearing a rosette of leaves and a tuft of roots, is found. In mint and jasmine a slender lateral branch arches downwards to touch the ground; in banana, pineapple and Chrysanthemum the lateral branches originate from the underground stem and come out obliquely upward.

options.en: A slender lateral branch that arches down to touch the ground
A lateral branch with short internodes, each node bearing a rosette of leaves and a tuft of roots
Underground lateral branches that grow obliquely upward

stem.en: In Opuntia, the flattened green structure that carries out photosynthesis is a modified:

explanation.en: Some plants of arid regions modify their stems into flattened (Opuntia) or fleshy cylindrical (Euphorbia) structures that contain chlorophyll and carry out photosynthesis. In Australian acacia it is the petiole that expands and turns green.

stem.en: How can a compound leaf be distinguished from a twig bearing simple leaves?

explanation.en: A bud is present in the axil of the petiole in both simple and compound leaves, but not in the axil of the leaflets of a compound leaf. A twig bearing simple leaves would have an axillary bud in each leaf axil.

options.en: A bud is present in the axil of each leaflet of a compound leaf
A bud is present in the axil of the petiole of a compound leaf but not in the axil of its leaflets
Leaflets of compound leaves are always opposite

stem.en: Long, thin, flexible petioles help leaf blades to:

explanation.en: The petiole helps hold the blade to light. Long thin flexible petioles allow leaf blades to flutter in the wind, thereby cooling the leaf and bringing fresh air to the leaf surface.

options.en: Flutter in the wind, thereby cooling the leaf and bringing fresh air to the leaf surface

stem.en: In Australian acacia, the leaves are small and short-lived. The function of photosynthesis is taken over by:

explanation.en: In Australian acacia the leaves are small and short-lived; the petioles expand, become green and synthesise food (phyllodes).

stem.en: A flower that can be divided into two similar halves only in one particular vertical plane is:

explanation.en: Such a flower is zygomorphic (bilaterally symmetrical), as in pea, gulmohur, bean and Cassia. An actinomorphic flower (mustard, datura, chilli) can be divided into equal halves by any radial plane through the centre; an asymmetric flower (canna) cannot be divided by any vertical plane.

stem.en: Perigynous flowers, in which the ovary is said to be half-inferior, are found in:

explanation.en: In perigynous flowers the gynoecium is situated in the centre and other parts are on the rim of the thalamus almost at the same level — plum, rose, peach. Mustard, china rose and brinjal are hypogynous (superior ovary); guava, cucumber and ray florets of sunflower are epigynous (inferior ovary).

stem.en: Monoadelphous, diadelphous and polyadelphous stamens are found respectively in:

explanation.en: Stamens united into one bunch (monoadelphous) — china rose; two bundles (diadelphous) — pea; more than two bundles (polyadelphous) — citrus.

stem.en: Marginal placentation, in which the placenta forms a ridge along the ventral suture and ovules are borne in two rows, is seen in:

explanation.en: Marginal placentation occurs in pea. Tomato, china rose and lemon show axile; mustard and Argemone show parietal; Dianthus and Primrose show free central placentation.

stem.en: In parietal placentation, as in mustard and Argemone:

explanation.en: In parietal placentation the ovules develop on the inner wall of the ovary or on the peripheral part. The ovary is one-chambered but becomes two-chambered due to the formation of a false septum (mustard, Argemone). The other options describe free central, basal and axile placentation.

options.en: Ovules are borne on a central axis and septa are absent
Ovules develop on the inner wall of the ovary; the one-chambered ovary becomes two-chambered due to a false septum
A single ovule is attached at the base
The placenta is axial in a multilocular ovary

stem.en: A fruit formed without fertilisation of the ovary is called:

explanation.en: The fruit is a mature or ripened ovary developed after fertilisation. If a fruit is formed without fertilisation of the ovary, it is called a parthenocarpic fruit. Drupe, legume and berry are fruit types formed after fertilisation.

stem.en: Which seed is endospermic (albuminous)?

explanation.en: In some seeds such as castor, the endosperm formed as a result of double fertilisation is a food-storing tissue — endospermic. In bean, gram and pea, the endosperm is not present in mature seeds — non-endospermous; food is stored in the cotyledons.

stem.en: In a maize grain, the plumule and the radicle are enclosed respectively in sheaths called:

explanation.en: In monocot seeds the embryo has a single large shield-shaped cotyledon, the scutellum, and a short axis with plumule and radicle. The plumule is enclosed in the coleoptile and the radicle in the coleorhiza. The first option reverses them. The aleurone layer is the proteinous outer layer of the endosperm.

stem.en: In Solanaceae, the placentation and the nature of stamens are:

explanation.en: In Solanaceae the gynoecium is bicarpellary, syncarpous, the ovary superior, bilocular, with a swollen placenta bearing many ovules (axile); the androecium has five epipetalous stamens. Marginal placentation with diadelphous stamens is the Fabaceae pattern.

options.en: Axile with swollen placenta; five epipetalous stamens

stem.en: Which of the following is a feature of Liliaceae?

explanation.en: Liliaceae: perianth tepal six (3+3), often united into a tube; valvate aestivation; stamens six (3+3), epitepalous; tricarpellary syncarpous superior trilocular ovary with axile placentation. Vexillary corolla and pulvinate leaf bases are Fabaceae features; an obliquely placed bicarpellary ovary is a Solanaceae feature.

options.en: Five free petals with vexillary aestivation
Perianth of six tepals (3+3) often united into a tube; stamens six, epitepalous

stem.en:
Statement I: In cereals such as maize, the seed coat is membranous and generally fused with the fruit wall.
Statement II: The outer covering of the endosperm, which separates it from the embryo, is a proteinous layer called the aleurone layer.

explanation.en: Both are correct NCERT lines. In maize the seed coat is membranous and fused with the fruit wall; the endosperm is bulky and stores food; the outer covering of the endosperm separates the embryo by a proteinous layer called the aleurone layer. The embryo lies in a groove at one end of the endosperm.

options.en: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct

stem.en: In vexillary aestivation of the pea flower:

explanation.en: In pea and bean flowers there are five petals: the largest (standard) overlaps the two lateral petals (wings), which in turn overlap the two smallest anterior petals (keel) — vexillary or papilionaceous aestivation. The third option describes valvate and the fourth twisted aestivation; the first reverses the order of overlap.

options.en: The two anterior petals (keel) overlap the two lateral petals (wings) which overlap the standard
The largest petal (standard) overlaps the two lateral petals (wings), which in turn overlap the two smallest anterior petals (keel)
All five petals just touch at the margins without overlap
Each petal overlaps the next one in one direction

stem.en: The floral formula of Fabaceae is written as % ⚥ K(5) C1+2+(2) A(9)+1 G1 (with G underlined). This tells us that:

explanation.en: % = zygomorphic; ⚥ = bisexual; K(5) = five united sepals; C1+2+(2) = standard, two wings, two fused keel petals; A(9)+1 = diadelphous stamens (nine fused + one free); G1 underlined = superior, monocarpellary ovary. A line under G shows a superior ovary; a line above would show an inferior ovary.

options.en: The flower is actinomorphic with ten free stamens and an inferior ovary
The flower is unisexual with polyadelphous stamens
The flower is zygomorphic and bisexual, with five united sepals, a corolla of one standard, two wings and two fused keel petals, diadelphous stamens and a superior monocarpellary ovary
The flower has a perianth of six tepals

stem.en:
Match the ovary position with an example:
(a) Hypogynous (b) Perigynous (c) Epigynous
(i) Guava (ii) Rose (iii) Mustard

explanation.en: Hypogynous (superior ovary) — mustard, china rose, brinjal. Perigynous (half-inferior) — plum, rose, peach. Epigynous (inferior ovary; thalamus grows up enclosing the ovary completely) — guava, cucumber, ray florets of sunflower.

stem.en:
Assertion (A): Leaves are arranged in an acropetal order on the stem.
Reason (R): Leaves originate from the shoot apical meristem.

explanation.en: Both true and R explains A. Leaves originate from shoot apical meristems and are therefore arranged in acropetal order (older leaves below, younger leaves towards the apex). Each leaf develops at a node and bears a bud in its axil.

options.en: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

stem.en:
Statement I: The flower is a modified shoot wherein the shoot apical meristem changes to a floral meristem.
Statement II: In a flower, the internodes elongate considerably and the axis becomes long.

explanation.en: Statement I is correct. Statement II is incorrect: in a flower, the internodes do not elongate and the axis gets condensed. The apex produces different kinds of floral appendages laterally at successive nodes instead of leaves.

options.en: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct

stem.en: Which pairing of plant and family is incorrect?

explanation.en: Muliathi is a medicine from Fabaceae, not Solanaceae. The others are correct: Indigofera (dye) — Fabaceae; ashwagandha and belladonna (medicines) — Solanaceae; colchicine from Colchicum autumnale — Liliaceae.

stem.en:
Assertion (A): In sunflower and marigold, the ovary contains a single ovule.
Reason (R): They show basal placentation, in which the placenta develops at the base of the ovary.

explanation.en: Both true and R explains A. In basal placentation the placenta develops at the base of the ovary and a single ovule is attached to it, as in sunflower and marigold.

options.en: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

stem.en:
Statement I: In monocotyledons, the leaf base expands into a sheath covering the stem partially or wholly.
Statement II: In some leguminous plants the leaf base becomes swollen, and is called the pulvinus.

explanation.en: Both statements are correct NCERT lines. The leaf base may bear two lateral small leaf-like structures called stipules; in monocots it expands into a sheath; in some legumes it is swollen into a pulvinus.

options.en: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
